topics.label: Lecture opening and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It frames the lecture series, introduces the subject of cancer biology, and outlines the session's learning outcomes.

topics.label: Cellular, genetic, and experimental foundations of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the genetic and developmental origins of cancer as a failure of tissue differentiation, along with the laboratory systems used to study it.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and histological progression
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the processes of invasion and metastasis and demonstrate how tumor progression is identified histologically.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and mechanisms of clinical pathogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how tumors are named and classified based on tissue origin and describe the physiological mechanisms through which neoplastic growths produce morbidity and mortality.

topics.label: Cancer incidence and patterns across species
topics.groupedBecause: They present the epidemiology, incidence rates, and mortality patterns of tumors across humans and comparative animal species.

topics.label: Cancer screening rationale, methods, and limitations
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate the clinical rationale for cancer screening and compare the diagnostic methods and efficacy of screening programs across different tumor types.

topics.label: Lecture close and practical preparation
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture by reiterating learning outcomes and outlining upcoming practical sessions.
